explanation: The conclusion `IsLocallyNormalRing S` is a predicate defined in this library (SchemeProperties/Normal.lean, line 98: every localization at a prime is a domain and integrally closed), not in Mathlib or Lean core: grep for `IsLocallyNormalRing` and even `LocallyNormal` over the whole Mathlib tree returns no matches. Consequently no Mathlib declaration can state this result. I also searched Mathlib for any statement of the shape 'an étale (or smooth) algebra over an integrally closed domain / normal ring is (locally) normal / integrally closed' — grepping Mathlib/RingTheory/Etale/*.lean and the whole of Mathlib for `Etale` together with `Normal`/`IntegrallyClosed`/`isIntegrallyClosed` produced nothing; the only relevant Mathlib inputs are the ingredients the proof actually uses (`Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod` in Mathlib/RingTheory/Etale/Field.lean, `TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure_bijective_of_smooth` in Mathlib/RingTheory/Smooth/IntegralClosure.lean, `IsIntegrallyClosed.integralClosure_eq_bot`), none of which comes close to the theorem itself. The library's own private helpers (`smooth_isIntegrallyClosedIn_baseChange_fraction`, `integralClosure_pi_fields_isLocallyNormal`) and the deprecated alias `IsLocallyNormalRing.of_finiteEtale_of_isDomain` are library declarations, so they do not count.
